No.37

Three Teachings the Bodhisattva Gave Me: Reflections on a Ten-Year Relationship

Three personal questions on love with the author's notes: meeting, owing, and after the affinity ends.

Author's record · translated; the Chinese original is authoritative

Open in reading mode →

🔶Inquiry to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

Only now can this humble student begin to face my past relationship honestly. I am grateful for the Bodhisattva's teachings all along, which gave me the courage to share them widely online. I also hope that all of you who read of my experience may come to sense the compassion of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and the truth of impermanence.

※ These are teachings for my own personal conditions. Conditions are countless; do not take one example as true for all under heaven. Please weigh them carefully as a reference.

[The Bodhisattva's teaching on publishing this text]

🔶The Bodhisattva's Teaching

"Good man,
your wish to circulate what you have recorded
is a praiseworthy intention;
yet know that once words go out,
a thousand people will understand them a thousand ways."
"If you wish to benefit beings,
let them grow in wisdom,
not in attachment."

"If you wish to speak of causes and conditions,
let beings know cause and effect,
not fatalism."
"What you have recorded
loses nothing of the main meaning;
the feelings you describe
are sincere and worthy."
"Yet remember:
this was spoken because of one person's suffering,
not as a law fixed for all people."

"Conditions are countless; do not take one example as true for all under heaven." "If you add one sentence so later readers know that their conditions differ, it will be more complete." "If you add one sentence so beings know that cultivating the heart matters more than seeking answers, it will accord better with the Dharma."

"When you publish,
seek no praise,
seek no approval,
seek no proof."
"May those who read it have a little less resentment
and a little more clarity;
a little less hatred,
a little more kindness."

"Circulated in this way,
it will bring benefit."
"With such an intention,
the effort will not be in vain."

Author's Note

(End of the Bodhisattva's guidance on publishing.)

==== Below are the teachings on my previous relationship ====

🔶Inquiry to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

First question: why, after ten years together, did it come to nothing?

🔶The Bodhisattva's Teaching

"Conditions arise not for the sake of an outcome,
and an outcome is not the original intent of the conditions.
Your meeting with them
was not the final station, but a point on the way.
Ten years were not wasted;
they let each heart know what it truly wished for.
Had you never met,
you would not know what you value;
had you not walked long together,
they would not know what they could not accept.

To walk together for a stretch in love
is already one kind of completeness;
it need not last to the end
to be called faithful."

🔶Inquiry to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

Second question: who owed whom?

🔶The Bodhisattva's Teaching

"Not owing,
nor repaying.
When conditions come,
they are not an ending,
but a revealing of the heart.
If you judge causes by suffering,
all conditions are mistakes;
if you judge causes by awakening,
all conditions are kindnesses.

You and they
did not come to wound each other,
but to reflect each other.
One saw clearly 'what I want',
the other saw clearly 'what I cannot do';
neither is a fault,
neither is a sin.
The wound came from not fitting together,
not from meeting.

Without this affinity,
you would still not know the weight of your own heart;
without this parting,
they would still not see the boundary they keep."

🔶Inquiry to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

Third question: would it have been better to end it earlier?

🔶The Bodhisattva's Teaching

"Neither early nor late;
it ends when the conditions ripen.
Had you ended it then,
with the heart not yet clear,
ending would have been fleeing;
were you to stay now,
with love already spent,
staying would become harm.

That you can stop now
is not late awakening,
but the arrival of the right conditions.
To insist on calling 'early' good
is to blame the past heart with hindsight —
neither wise
nor kind.
Their pain now
is not because you ended it late,
but because the feelings were not yet spent;
your pain now
is not because of when it ended,
but because your heart is still kind."

Author's Note

(The three questions are finished. My own reflections follow.)

Personal note
We should know that what is called "letting go" —
is not asking you to forget the past;
is not asking you to deny the past;
is not asking you to force yourself to cut off all feeling.
Rather — it is no longer letting past events bind your present heart.

This teaching does not tell everyone that "relationships need not be cherished", and still less does it encourage giving up when things are hard. Quite the opposite: precisely because I once gave sincerely, I can look back with a clear conscience even though the affinity has ended. If the affinity remains, cherish and tend it; if the affinity has ended, learn to let go. Perhaps this is the lesson that causes and conditions have taught me.

I make these teachings public not to complain, nor to blame anyone, but because I know that many people in the world, like me, blame themselves after a parting and keep chewing over "if only" in their memories. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's teaching did not give me an "answer", but it gave me a "direction" — no longer asking who was right or wrong, but asking myself: what did this meeting teach me?

That learning is the greatest blessing of my life.
